ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g4-arts-music-u03-l03

Lesson focus: dynamics and tempo

Resource type: ACADEMY_CREATED_SCAFFOLD

GUIDED SCAFFOLD A — first supported pass for dynamics and tempo. 1 INTENT: name what the study should do. 2 SETUP: choose a safe, available route. 3 NOTICE: locate rhythm, contour, harmony, texture, form, dynamics, timbre, and phrase structure. 4 ACT: complete one small study using this cue—A repeated idea creates recognition; contrast changes expectation; return lets the listener compare what changed. Notation or an event map preserves those decisions for checking. 5 CHECK: point to the result before using “works” or “does not work.” 6 SECOND STUDY: change one relationship only. Keep both attempts and circle the exact prompt you are ready to remove. Worked example for dynamics and tempo: An A–B–A plan can keep the pulse constant, change texture in B, and return to A more softly so the return is recognizable but not copied exactly. Use it to study dynamics and tempo; describe evidence before judging and adapt the demonstrated relationship rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Manuel Academy resource in this package. It gives you the model, example, or help sheet needed for this task.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Tap, point through, gesture, or use the supplied notation or event map without recording. A written or notated response can show structure and reasoning; it does not claim hearing or performed control that was not actually demonstrated. No instrument, microphone, camera, or public performance is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task uses sound (dynamics and tempo). You do not have to hear it to do it. You may use a written or drawn version, feel the beat by tapping or watching, or read the notes on paper instead.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
No public performance, voice recording, photo, or camera use is ever required; provide a private, written, or no-audio alternative for every task.
Use only original student work, public-domain material, or properly licensed excerpts; never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or protected works.
The final product must remain the student’s own authorship; adult or AI assistance may support planning and feedback but must not create the graded work.

media.fallback: Count, point through, tap, speak, gesture, or read the complete pulse and pitch map silently; no instrument, speaker, microphone, or recording is required.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce dynamics and tempo to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one rhythm relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact rhythm evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from rhythm, contour, harmony, texture, form, dynamics, timbre, and phrase structure; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply dynamics and tempo under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on dynamics and tempo rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_instruction.title: What dynamics and tempo means here
concept_instruction.body: Musical structure is the pattern of repetition, contrast, layering, and return that makes events relate across time.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: A repeated idea creates recognition; contrast changes expectation; return lets the listener compare what changed. Notation or an event map preserves those decisions for checking.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: More layers can enrich texture but hide a main idea. More repetition can create coherence but become predictable without meaningful variation. Worked example: An A–B–A plan can keep the pulse constant, change texture in B, and return to A more softly so the return is recognizable but not copied exactly. Non-example: Adding unrelated events without a preserved pattern makes the form difficult to hear or verify.
